title: private-deploy-networking-breadcrumbs
content:
Quick scratchpad for the customer private deployment networking flakiness (notes + commands tried + hypotheses).

Context:
- Customer: acme-medical (private deployment, VPC peered to Redwood-prod-vpc)
- Deployment ID: private-acme-2026-02
- Reporter: customer SRE via CS-1427; intermittent 502/SSL errors when calling model endpoint from customer subnets.
- Infra: AWS (us-west-2) peering to Redwood-managed VPC; k8s nodes in customer subnet run sidecar egress gateway.

Observed symptoms (timeline):
- 2026-02-24 14:05 UTC: customer reports TLS handshake failures from app -> endpoint (ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR).
- 2026-02-24 14:17 UTC: same client sees NXDOMAIN for internal service-hostname during short window.
- 2026-02-24 14:20 UTC: requests that hit experimental fallback model return 502 Bad Gateway.
- 2026-02-25 09:30 UTC: we observed increased SYN_RECV -> RST counts in VPC flow logs for SG egress to 3.212.45.0/24 (redwood egress pool).

Commands / checks I've run (raw):
- Check VPC peering status (AWS CLI):
  aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=tag:Deployment,Values=private-acme-2026-02
  -> Status: active, AccepterVpcInfo.CidrBlock: 10.10.0.0/16, RequesterVpcInfo.CidrBlock: 10.20.0.0/16

- Route tables on customer VPC:
  aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0acmecust
  -> Found route to peer: DestinationCidrBlock=10.0.0.0/8 target=pcx-0abcde (looks broad)
  NOTE: double-check there are no overlapping routes from on-prem VPN that could steal 10.0.0.0/8

- VPC Flow Logs sample (pulled from cloudwatch):
  2026-02-24T14:18:03Z eni-0a1 10.20.12.45 3.212.45.12 443 54321 6 14 584 ACCEPT OK
  2026-02-24T14:18:04Z eni-0a1 10.20.12.45 3.212.45.12 443 54322 6 0 0 REJECT NACL
  -> intermittent REJECTs from NACL? Port 443 sometimes allowed, sometimes denied based on ephemeral port? suspicious

- DNS checks from customer host (nslookup / dig):
  dig +short model-svc.private.redwood.internal @10.20.0.2
  -> sometimes returns 10.30.5.12, sometimes NXDOMAIN
  dig +trace model-svc.private.redwood.internal
  -> shows conditional-forwarder to 10.20.0.2 (customer resolver) then to 10.50.0.5 (redwood resolver). Timeout in one trace leg.

- TLS client error (curl):
  curl -v https://model-svc.private.redwood.internal/predict 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
  ->* Connected to model-svc.private.redwood.internal (3.212.45.12) port 443 (#0)
  ->* TLS handshake timeout
  ->* Closing connection 0

- From Redwood side: checked ingress ELB / ALB target health (redwood-managed):
  aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:us-west-2:111:tg/xx
  -> some targets Unhealthy with reason: TLS alert handshake_failure, others healthy

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Intermittent NACL / route table rule overlap causing some flows to be rejected (matches flow logs showing ACCEPT/REJECT for same src/dst).
2) DNS conditional forwarder flapping between customer resolver and redwood resolver causing NXDOMAIN intermittency -> client picks wrong IP (old/rotated) -> TLS IP mismatch.
3) Client-side egress proxy (sidecar) sometimes using wrong source IP (no reverse DNS / certificate SNI mismatch) -> ALB rejects handshake.
4) MTU / fragmentation issues (rare) causing TLS handshake to fail partway.

Notes / clues: 
- NACL on customer side is stateful? (NACLs are stateless) The pattern of ephemeral port being blocked fits stateless NACL misconfiguration \u2014 see REJECT in flow logs.
- Route table has very broad 10.0.0.0/8 pointing to peering; customer also runs a VPN to on-prem announcing 10.0.0.0/8 -> potential asymmetry where some packets route to on-prem and never return via peering.
- ALB logs show SNI=empty in some failed TLS attempts; suggests client didn't send SNI (older TLS stack or proxy stripping).

Immediate remediation attempts tried: 
- Asked customer to temporarily open wide egress (allow 3.212.45.0/24 all TCP ephemeral ports) -> reduced failures for 1hr during test window.
- Re-created a specific route for Redwood CIDR (10.30.0.0/16 -> pcx-0abcde) instead of broad 10.0.0.0/8; asked customer to remove overlapping VPN announcement.
- Flushed iptables and restarted sidecar on one node (kubectl exec -> systemctl restart egress-proxy) -> that node stable afterwards.

What I still need to validate: 
- Confirm if NACL rule change correlates exactly with timestamps (customer to pull config change logs).
- Capture tcpdump on customer host and on redwood ingress (paired timestamps) to see whether SYN/SYN-ACK path asymmetric.
- Reproduce DNS flip: capture queries and see TTLs for model-svc.private.redwood.internal; check if both resolvers return different answers with similar TTLs.
- Check ALB access logs for Client TLS version / SNI / cipher suites when handshake_failure occurred.

Next concrete steps (TODO):
- [ ] Get customer to enable VPC Flow Logs with full sample for 2026-02-24 13:50-15:00 and share logs link.
- [ ] Ask networking to run BGP route table dump on customer VPN appliance to check for 10.0.0.0/8 announcement. (ticket: infra-net-521)
- [ ] Instrument sidecar to log SNI for outbound TLS and client cert (if any).
- [ ] Add temporary CloudWatch metric alert for ALB TLS handshake_failure spikes for this deployment to catch events in real time.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight; paste interesting log lines into CS ticket. If this shows pattern of VPN/route overlap, we should add a note to the private deploy checklist: "don't announce broad RFC1918 ranges over BGP when peering."

Slack breadcrumbs / references: 
- Slack thread with customer SRE: https://slack-redwood.internal/archives/C01234567/p1623456789000
- Internal thread: #private-deploy-ops (see pinned msg 2026-02-24)

If stuck: escalate to infra-net with tcpdump pair (customer + redwood) + set a short maintenance window to force route change and test.

-- Jordan
